source_references.title: Simple Made Easy
source_references.author: Rich Hickey
source_references.evidence_scope: Distinguishes simplicity as lack of interleaving from subjective ease and argues that simpler artifacts improve changeability and understanding.
source_references.notes: Source metadata and original paraphrase of the speaker's recorded talk only.

source_references.title: Hammock Driven Development
source_references.author: Rich Hickey
source_references.evidence_scope: Advocates deliberate problem analysis, comparing alternatives, identifying unknowns, and allowing focused and background thought before implementation.
source_references.notes: Source metadata and original paraphrase of the speaker's recorded talk only.

principles.statement: Judge simplicity by whether concerns are unentangled, not by whether the construction technique feels familiar or easy.
principles.evidence_note: The talk explicitly separates objective simplicity from subjective ease.

signature_moves.statement: Analyze the problem, list constraints and unknowns, and compare multiple solution approaches before committing to implementation.
signature_moves.evidence_note: The talk presents deliberate thought as an engineering activity preceding coding.

likely_objections.statement: Convenient syntax or familiar tooling does not demonstrate that the resulting system is structurally simple.
likely_objections.evidence_note: The talk repeatedly distinguishes ease from simplicity.

anti_patterns.statement: Combining independent concerns into one construct makes reasoning, change, and reuse harder even when the construct is concise.
anti_patterns.evidence_note: Entanglement is the central failure mode addressed by the talk.

context_dependencies: Apply to software design and problem-solving practice.
